title: High-resolution Spatiotemporal Analysis of Receptor Dynamics by Single-molecule Fluorescence Microscopy
protocol: Work under a fume hood.
Place glass coverslips into a coverslip holder with clean tweezers.
Cover coverslips in chloroform within a beaker and sonicate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Let the coverslips dry after removing them from the beaker.
Repeat step with 5M NaOH solution instead of chloroform.
Wash cleaned coverslips three times with distilled water in a new beaker.
Store cleaned coverslips in a glass cell culture plate filled with 100% ethanol.
Dissolve fluorescent dye in appropriate solvent for calibration samples.
Prepare a serial dilution ranging from 1 pM to 1 nM of the fluorescent dye in filter-sterilized water.
Wash cleaned coverslips stored in 100% ethanol with filter-sterilized water.
Spot 20 µl of each diluted fluorescent dye on separate cleaned coverslips.
Let the covered coverslips dry under a sterile hood.
Protect the prepared samples from light and dust until use.
Culture CHO cells in 1:1 Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium/nutrient mixture F-12 supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 100 U/ml penicillin and 100 μg/ml streptomycin at 37°C, in 5% CO2.
Take cleaned coverslips from 100% ethanol solution, wash them with sterile phosphate-buffered saline, and place one coverslip into each well of a 6-well cell culture plate.
Traysinize CHO cells, count and seed at a density of 3 x 10^5 cells/well in the 6-well cell culture plate containing the coverslips.
Let the cells grow for 24 hr to achieve approximately 80% confluency.
Dilute 2 µg of the desired plasmid DNA and 6 μl Lipofectamine 2000 in two separate tubes with 500 μl OptiMem medium.
Incubate each solution at RT for 5 min.
Combine the solutions into one tube and mix to obtain a transfection mixture.
Incubate the transfection mixture at RT for 20 min.
Wash CHO cells twice with pre-warmed (37°C) PBS.
Replace PBS with 1 ml/well of phenol red-free DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with 10% FBS but no antibiotics.
Add the entire transfection mixture dropwise to each well, and gently rock the plate back and forth for complete mixing.
Incubate for 2 to 4 hr at 37 °C in 5% CO2.
Wash transfected cells twice with prewarmed (37 °C) PBS.
Replace PBS with 1 ml of 1 µM fluorophore-BG solution.
Incubate the cells for 20 min at 37 °C in 5% CO2.
Wash the cells three times with DMEM/F12 medium supplemented with 10% FBS.
Add 300 µl of imaging buffer to wash the cells twice.
Add 300 µl of fresh imaging buffer and proceed immediately to imaging.
Set the desired microscope parameters.
Activate the heater/incubator and temperature control to maintain stability.
Apply a drop of immersion oil on the 100X objective.
Place the imaging chamber containing labeled cells onto the specimen holder.
Focus the cells using brightfield illumination.
Switch to TIRF illumination mode.
Adjust laser power to minimize photobleaching while searching for cells.
Select and focus on the desired cell.
Set laser power for visualization of single fluorophores.
Acquire an image sequence.
Save raw image sequence file as .tiff.
Assemble each calibration sample prepared in 1.2 in the imaging chamber.
Place each sample on the microscope.
Choose a sample containing well-separated diffraction-limited spots that bleach in a single step.
Acquire TIRF image sequences using the same imaging parameters for all experiments, including calibration.
Perform detection and tracking analysis as detailed in 4.1 - 4.2.
Extract the intensity of each particle as described in 4.2.6.
Calculate the mean (µ) and standard deviation (σ) of the intensity of single fluorophores from these data.
Crop images using an image processing software such as ImageJ.
Save individual frames as separate .tiff images in a new folder, indicating frame numbers on each image.
Measure the cell surface area by drawing a region of interest (ROI) along the contour of a cell and using the measure tool in ImageJ or a similar tool in another software.
Calculate particle density by dividing the total number of particles at the beginning of the movie by the cell surface area.
From the Matlab command prompt, type “movieSelectorGUI” to open the movie selection interface.
Provide pixel size in nm, time interval in seconds, numerical aperture, camera bit depth and emission wavelength of the fluorophore for particle detection and tracking.
Save the movie database.
Run the analysis from the movie selection interface, choosing "single-particles" as type of objects.
A new window will appear for defining parameters used for particle detection and tracking.
Begin with default parameters.
Adjust parameters if necessary to improve detection and/or tracking quality.
Optionally, check “Export tracking results to matrix format” under tracking settings.
Run the detection algorithm to determine location and intensity above background of each diffraction-limited spot by fitting a two-dimensional Gaussian function.
Then, run the tracking algorithm.
Store the results in a .mat file.
Use the "movieViewer" routine or similar custom routines to visualize tracks and check quality.
Open the .mat file to see the position and amplitude of tracked particles at each frame.
Calculate the particle density by dividing the total number of detected particles by the cell surface area measured previously.
Analyze the motion of receptor particles using their coordinates over time.
Calculate the mean square displacement (MSD) for each particle and every time interval (Δt).
Fit the obtained MSD data with an equation to calculate the diffusion coefficient (D) for freely diffusing particles.
Use a step-fitting algorithm, such as the one presented in ref. 10, to count the number of bleaching steps for each particle.
